key_insight: CodeRescue shows that in coding agents, failed executions are not dead ends—they provide feedback that can justify additional low-cost recovery attempts before escalating to a stronger model. The key breakthrough is a budget-calibrated routing strategy that decides when to keep trying cheap repairs versus when to spend on expensive escalation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of allocating inference budget in coding agents that work in executable environments. Existing cost-aware systems usually follow a simple cascade pattern, but they do not account for the value of execution feedback that can make repeated cheap-model recovery effective.
method: Uses execution feedback from failed code runs as signal for whether further recovery attempts are likely to succeed.
Learns or designs a routing policy that balances repeated low-cost repair attempts against escalation to a higher-capability, higher-cost model.
Optimizes decision-making under a fixed budget to improve success rates without unnecessary expensive calls.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building coding assistants, this work offers a more practical way to trade off cost and reliability. It can reduce spending on large models while still improving repair performance in agentic coding workflows.
visual_elements: A flowchart showing: code attempt -> execution feedback -> cheap recovery loop -> escalation to strong model

paper_title: CodeRescue: Budget-Calibrated Recovery Routing for Coding Agents
paper_authors: Qijia He, Jiayi Cheng, Chenqian Le, Rui Wang, Xunmei Liu
